_comment: CAPABILITY suite for the MySQL CDC stream source with initial_load UNDER LIVE CHANGES, over every table of the employeescdc model -- one table per way a row is identified: accounts (a primary key every update CHANGES: the before-image must carry the old key, the row the new), ledger (a composite primary key), devices (no primary key, a unique index), readings (no primary key and no index) -- and its xp_sentinel (functions/caps_mysqlcdc_initial_load.py::mysqlcdc_initial_load_live). The same stages as postgrescdc_initial_load_live: (1) domains -- create the mysqlcdc domain, install the employeescdc model, load the m seed (10k rows a table), its operations appended to ${xp:dir}/ops.jsonl (--emit-ops) -- as every data command below appends its own; (2) actions, tagged live -- `sentinel-data --key after-create-data`, then start `churn` in the background: 20 passes a second apart, `modify-data --ops Mix --sets 250` -- ~1000 CDC rows each: every set one transaction of one verb over all four tables, inserts, updates (accounts' moving its key) and deletes; nothing cascades; it keeps running through the stages below; (3) collections; (4) functions -- register the @stream_publisher, which STARTS it: its snapshot is taken over tables changing under it, and every change after it arrives as a CDC row, over the binlog, from the GTID position the snapshot's brief global read lock pinned (server_id 812 for this suite, 813 for the other, so both run at once); (5) actions, tagged live -- wait for churn to finish, then `sentinel-data --key after-churn`; (6) sentinel -- hold until both keys are in xp_sentinel_changes (at most 5m each); (7) actions, tagged check -- scripts/verify_cdc_ops.py --check state checks what a target would hold: the snapshot plus every <table>_changes applied in order as the connector deduplicates (an insert when its key has no row, an update or delete when it has one), each table ending as the whole ops.jsonl leaves it -- a snapshot taken under changes has no one point the trail splits at, so the changes are not paired one by one; with no table --keyless, any change the snapshot already holds fails the check: the snapshot is one point in time; (8) monitor. Run: `tdd xp one-shot --suite container-connectors/mysqlcdc_initial_load_live --keep`. verify-ops runs with --cascades unlogged --noops unlogged: the binlog has no row event for what a cascade takes (InnoDB applies it below the binlog) nor for a row an UPDATE did not change, so none may arrive.
